Title: Design 4, The ledger: Mistral, a European brain
Language: en-GB

The ledger
 Does sovereignty matter to you? Five questions
 Sovereign means you can choose, and change, who runs your model. Answer for the AI you use today.
 Your set-up
 Who holds the keys? Choose I do A provider does Not sure 
 Where does it run? Choose On my own device In the EU Outside the EU Not sure 
 Which licence? Choose Apache 2.0 or as open Restricted or closed Not sure 
 How long is data kept? Choose Not kept, or by me only A stated period Not stated Not sure 
 Can you leave? Choose Yes: change the address Only with real work No Not sure 
 Your tally
 Answer the five questions and your tally appears here. 
 Worked out in this page, in your browser. Nothing you choose is sent anywhere or stored.
 Not sure of an answer? The worked example below shows where to look.
 The worked example: Mistral’s three levels
 Every cell sourced, as read on 20 November 2026.
 Five questions, answered for Mistral on the device, in the EU and through any provider 
 Set-up Who holds the keys? Where does it run? Which licence? How long is data kept? Can you leave? 
 On the device Ministral 3, run locally You. A local model needs no API key. On your own hardware. Whether a Pi or a tablet is enough is an estimate, not measured.⁠ 1 Apache 2.0.⁠ 2 On your disk, for as long as you keep it. Yes: the same OpenAI-style call as the others.⁠ 3 
 Mistral, in the EU Mistral’s API, your key You hold your API key; Mistral runs the model. Hosted in the EEA by default⁠ 4 ; processed in the EU only on the EU endpoint, at 1.1 times the price.⁠ 5 Some features may use subprocessors outside the EU.⁠ 6 Apache 2.0 for Ministral 3 and Mistral Small 4; Mistral Large 4 has a modified MIT licence whose condition Mistral’s pages describe two ways.⁠ 7 30 rolling days for abuse monitoring, unless zero data retention is on (pay-as-you-go, stateless calls, on request); Agents API data until the account ends.⁠ 8 Yes: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (in public preview), like local servers and OpenRouter.⁠ 9 
 Any provider OpenRouter, your key You hold your OpenRouter key; the provider runs the model.⁠ 10 Wherever that provider runs. Read its terms. Depends on the model you pick. Set by OpenRouter’s and the provider’s terms; not read here for every provider. Yes: change the address and the model name.

 Mistral’s inference page says “Data sent through our API isn’t used for model training”, but its help centre says that in Free mode it may use API inputs and outputs for training unless you opt out (a toggle in the Admin panel, under Privacy), and that Labs and Public Preview models may be used for training whatever the plan.⁠ 11 
 Mistral says it “complies with both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001/27701 frameworks”.⁠ 12

Title: Design 2, The map: Mistral, a European brain
Language: en-GB
Path: /designs/2.html

The map
 Where your words go
 When a sovereign website asks a model to write, your brief has to go somewhere. There are three places it can go. This drawing uses only what the providers publish, as read on 20 November 2026.
 Sovereign means you can choose, and change, who runs your model. The ledger asks five questions of any AI you depend on. 
 Three paths, one interface: the same OpenAI-style call, with a different address.⁠ 1 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 Mistral docs, Chat completion · Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility · OpenRouter, Quickstart 
 Pick a path
 1 On your device
 What is sent
 Your brief, to a model on your own machine. After the model is downloaded, nothing needs to leave it.
 To whom
 No one else. For example Ministral 3 run by Ollama. Ollama serves an OpenAI-style endpoint at http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions .⁠ 2 
 What is kept
 Whatever you keep, on your own disk.
 The model
 Ministral 3 was announced on 2 December 2025 in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes, for edge and local use, each with image understanding, under Apache 2.0.⁠ 3 
 Will it fit
 An estimate, not measured. The article estimates that the 3B and 8B, compressed to about 2 to 5GB, should run on a 16GB Raspberry Pi 5, the 8B slowly; on a tablet, the 3B is the realistic one.⁠ 4 Mistral’s official compressed (Q4_K_M) files are 2.15 GB for the 3B and 5.20 GB for the 8B, plus about 0.85 GB for vision. Those are download sizes, not memory use or speed.⁠ 5 
 Open the on-device demo 
 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility 
 Mistral AI, Mistral 3 
 A European brain for a sovereign website (Dinis Cruz, SGit Newsroom) 
 Hugging Face, Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512-GGUF · Hugging Face, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-GGUF 
 2 To Mistral, in the EU
 What is sent
 Your brief and your own API key, to Mistral’s API: for processing in the EU, to its EU endpoint.
 To whom
 Mistral AI was founded in April 2023, and describes itself as “a European leader” in AI.⁠ 6 
 Where
 By default, data is hosted in the EEA.⁠ 7 Hosting is not processing: Mistral does not commit to an inference location on the global endpoint, api.mistral.ai . Processing in the EU needs the EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai , billed at 1.1 times list price, without Agents, Batch or the Files API, and serving only the models hosted there.⁠ 8 Mistral’s regional endpoints were announced as generally available on 11 August 2026.⁠ 9 Some features may move data temporarily outside the EU to listed subprocessors; Enterprise customers can switch some of these off.⁠ 10 
 What is kept, how long
 API inputs and outputs are kept for 30 rolling days to monitor abuse, unless zero data retention is on; Agents API data is kept until the account ends. Zero data retention is only for pay-as-you-go, only for stateless calls, must be requested and may be refused, and does not cover Labs or Public Preview models.⁠ 11 
 Training
 Mistral’s inference page says “Data sent through our API isn’t used for model training”, but its help centre says that in Free mode it may use API inputs and outputs for training unless you opt out (a toggle in the Admin panel, under Privacy), and that Labs and Public Preview models may be used for training whatever the plan.⁠ 12 
 Run it side by side 
 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 Mistral AI, About 
 Mistral help centre, Where do you store my data 
 Mistral docs, Regional inference 
 Mistral AI, Regional inference announcement 
 Mistral help centre, Where do you store my data 
 Mistral AI, Privacy policy · Mistral help centre, Zero data retention · Mistral docs, Zero data retention 
 Mistral AI, Cloud inference · Mistral help centre, Do you use my data to train · Mistral help centre, Opting out of training 
 3 To any provider, with your key
 What is sent
 Your brief and your own key, to OpenRouter, which passes the brief to the provider of the model you pick.
 To whom
 OpenRouter, then that provider. OpenRouter’s OpenAI-style API is at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 .⁠ 13 
 What is kept, how long
 Set by OpenRouter’s terms and the provider’s. This site has not read them for every provider, so it does not say.
 Why it matters
 Leaving is changing an address, not rebuilding the site.
 Your key, and where it goes 
 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 OpenRouter, Quickstart 
 Before you pick
 Ministral 3, Mistral Small 4 and Voxtral Small are labelled Apache 2.0. Mistral Large 4 is under a modified MIT licence: its announcement says a company offering it as a model-as-a-service needs a separate commercial licence, while Mistral’s help centre describes the condition as a monthly revenue threshold of 20 million dollars. The pages disagree; read the licence file itself before relying on either.⁠ 14 
 The idea of a Mistral default on every sovereign website is a proposal from Dinis Cruz’s article A European brain for a sovereign website . Nothing has been agreed with Mistral.
